Klwow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Klwów, Poland

Demolished. Jews are recorded in Klwów from the 1760s, owning 13 houses in the village by 1787; by 1921 the town's 297 Jewish residents made up nearly a third of the population. In October 1941, Klwów's Jews were forced into the ghetto at Drzewica, and deported to Treblinka the following year. The cemetery itself, on the road toward Głuszyna, dates to the 18th century and was destroyed during World War II; no gravestones survive, and the isolated flat plot today carries no sign or marker of its former use.
